'''''Pleroma urvilleanum''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Tibouchina urvilleana''''',<ref name=POWO_77206410-1/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Melastomataceae, [[native plant|native]] to Brazil.

[[Common name]]s include:
{{div col | colwidth = 15em}}
*'''glory bush'''
*'''lasiandra'''<ref name="RHSPS">{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/18220/Tibouchina-urvilleana/Details|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Tibouchina urvilleana''|accessdate=12 March 2021}}</ref>
*'''princess flower'''
*'''pleroma'''
*'''purple glory tree'''<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref>
{{div col end}}
The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''urvilleanum'' commemorates the 19th-century French explorer and botanist [[Jules Dumont d'Urville]].<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref>

==Description==
Growing to {{convert|3|-|6|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|2|-|3|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} wide, it is a sprawling [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] with longitudinally veined, dark green hairy leaves. Clusters of brilliant purple flowers up to {{convert|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, with black stamens, are borne throughout summer and autumn.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
Under the synonym ''Tibouchina urvilleana'', ''Pleroma urvilleanum'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="RHSPS" /><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 102 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 23 December 2018}}</ref>

With a minimum temperature of {{convert|3|C|F|abbr=on}}, it requires some winter protection, and in [[temperateness|temperate]] areas is often grown in a conservatory. However, it can also be grown outside in a sunny, sheltered spot.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/st633|title=ENH791/ST633: ''Tibouchina urvilleana'': Princess Flower}}</ref> Plants are best grown in acidic and well-drained soils and spread by suckers. It can be trained as a vine and grown on a trellis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282684&isprofile=0&|title=Tibouchina urvilleana - Plant Finder|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org|language=en-US|access-date=2018-07-03}}</ref>
